entities.name: The Analects (Lunyu)
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
A collection of sayings, dialogues, and brief narratives attributed to Confucius and his disciples, compiled after his death (c. 5th–3rd century BCE) in 20 chapters (pian) comprising 497 passages. The Analects is the single most influential text in Chinese history and one of the most important philosophical works in world literature. Its teachings on benevolence (ren — "Do not do to others what you would not wish done to yourself"), ritual propriety (li), filial piety (xiao), the ideal "gentleman" (junzi), and virtuous governance became the moral and political foundation of Chinese civilization.

From the Song dynasty onward (960 CE), the Analects was one of the Four Books that formed the core curriculum for the imperial examination system, meaning that every educated Chinese person for nearly a millennium committed its contents to memory.
